context.requirement_text:
Closes the layering and restart-intensity portions of ISS-0425/GH#829
(queue task 425), sized per ISSUE-FIXER's own diagnosis
(handoffs/WF03-ISS0425-20260903/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnosis.json):
Letflow.Application.start/2 (lib/letflow/application.ex:26-139, read
2026-09-03) builds ONE flat list of 20 children -- Letflow.Repo,
Ecto.Migrator, Oidcc.ProviderConfiguration.Worker, Letflow.Registry,
Letflow.Metrics.Registry, Letflow.Admission (REQ-216),
Letflow.InstanceSupervisor, 7 Task.Supervisors (SandboxPool, Plugin,
Lua, Wasm.ModuleRegistry, Wasm.CapabilityGate,
Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistry, Obs.Alerts), Letflow.SandboxPool,
Letflow.Engine.PluginRegistry, Letflow.Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistry,
Letflow.Scheduler.Poller (REQ-186, gated :start_scheduler),
Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller (REQ-214, gated
:start_service_task_dispatcher), and Bandit (gated :start_http) -- all
as peers under one `Supervisor.start_link(children, strategy:
:one_for_one, name: Letflow.Supervisor)` with no
max_restarts/max_seconds override (OTP default: 3 restarts/5s).
DOCUMENTED, NON-HYPOTHETICAL INCIDENT THIS REQUIREMENT MUST MAKE
STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: scheduler_children/0's own comment
(application.ex:154-172) and ISS-0421 both describe a Poller whose
zero-delay first tick (`Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 0)`) raises
DBConnection.OwnershipError repeatedly under Ecto sandbox mode until
the shared top-level supervisor's restart intensity is exceeded and
the WHOLE application -- Letflow.Repo and Bandit included -- shuts
down. REQ-214's ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller (application.ex:181-197)
documents the IDENTICAL hazard for a second, independent poller. Both
are currently worked around only by disabling them under test
(config/test.exs), not by any structural isolation -- a real
production crash-loop in either poller still takes the whole node
down today.
DECISIONS (settled here, not left to CODE-DESIGNER, per this
project's own REQ-216/217/218 design-gate precedent of resolving
real open questions at the requirement stage):
1. TOP-LEVEL SHAPE: three new sibling supervisor modules under
lib/letflow/supervisor/ -- Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure,
Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, Letflow.Supervisor.Http (each `use
Supervisor`, own start_link/1 and init/1) -- become the ONLY 3
children of Letflow.Application's own Supervisor.start_link/2 call,
under strategy: :one_for_one (NOT :rest_for_one, deliberately
diverging from ISS-0425's own "candidate shape" text: ISSUE-FIXER's
diagnosis names the concrete reason -- :rest_for_one at the top would
cascade-restart every LATER-listed layer whenever an EARLIER one's
supervisor exits, e.g. a rare Infrastructure exit would force-restart
Pollers AND Http even though neither holds a pid-based dependency on
any Infrastructure child, since every named-process infra child
(Repo, both Registries, all 7 Task.Supervisors, InstanceSupervisor)
is looked up BY NAME at each call site, never by stored pid).
:one_for_one at the top means a Pollers crash-loop exhausting ITS OWN
restart intensity kills and restarts ONLY Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers
-- Infrastructure (Repo included) and Http are never touched. This is
the structural fix for the documented incident above.
2. LAYER MEMBERSHIP (every one of the 20 current children assigned):
Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure owns, in EXACTLY their current
relative order (preserving both hand-maintained ordering constraints
below as a property of Supervisor's own sequential per-child startup,
not a comment): Letflow.Repo, Ecto.Migrator,
Oidcc.ProviderConfiguration.Worker, Letflow.Registry,
Letflow.Metrics.Registry, Letflow.Admission, Letflow.InstanceSupervisor,
SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor, Letflow.SandboxPool,
Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor, Engine.PluginRegistry,
Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor,
Engine.Wasm.CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor,
Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistry,
Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistryTaskSupervisor,
Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor -- strategy: :one_for_one, OTP default
restart intensity (crash-looping infra, e.g. Repo itself, indicates a
fault severe enough that taking the whole app down is still the
correct behavior; this requirement does not change that). Letflow.
Supervisor.Pollers owns Letflow.Scheduler.Poller and
Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller (each still individually
gated by its own existing :start_scheduler /
:start_service_task_dispatcher config key -- an empty children list
when both are false, as under config/test.exs today, must start and
run without error). Letflow.Supervisor.Http owns Bandit (still gated
by :start_http).
3. RESTART INTENSITY PER LAYER: Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure and
Letflow.Supervisor.Http keep the OTP default (3 restarts/5s) -- no
documented incident motivates changing either. Letflow.
Supervisor.Pollers gets an EXPLICIT override, looser than the OTP
default to tolerate a handful of transient per-tick failures (a
single bad HTTP dispatch, a single locked row) without exiting:
max_restarts: 5, max_seconds: 60, recorded with this rationale in the
module's own moduledoc. Whichever value is chosen, the requirement's
AC4 below is the real bar -- a sustained crash-loop must still
exceed it and cause Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers (only) to exit and be
restarted once by the top-level Letflow.Supervisor.
4. ORDERING CONSTRAINTS PRESERVED (verified in application.ex as of
2026-09-03, both currently comment-enforced only): (a) ISS-0224 --
SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor before {Letflow.SandboxPool, []}, within
Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure's own list, unchanged relative
order; (b) ISS-0429 -- Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor before either
Poller's first tick can reach it, now structural: Letflow.
Supervisor.Infrastructure completes its ENTIRE startup (Supervisor's
own guarantee: each child's init/1 returns before the next child
starts) before Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers starts at all, which is a
strictly stronger guarantee than list-position-within-one-flat-list.
SEQUENCING NOTE FOR ISS-0421: ISS-0421 (Scheduler.Poller SPOF, 7
serial per-tenant sweeps) is explicitly waiting on this requirement
to settle restart-intensity policy before it decides its own,
narrower, Poller-internal fix (per both issues' own text: "whichever
runs second reads the other's outcome"). This requirement's decision
3 above (Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers: max_restarts 5, max_seconds 60)
is that settled input; ISS-0421's own fix must build on it, not
re-decide a conflicting intensity policy.
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT, AND WHY:
(a) ISS-0421's own internal Poller fix (bounding the 7 serial
per-tenant sweeps, e.g. via Task.async_stream) -- separate, narrower,
sequenced to land after this requirement per both issues' own text.
(b) ISS-0422's CLAUDE.md/requirements.yaml wording drift -- confirmed
documentation-only and unrelated; not touched here.
(c) The Task.Supervisor sprawl review (ISS-0425 part 3) -- REQ-220.
(d) Reversing REQ-045's row-based-instance decision, or giving
Letflow.InstanceSupervisor real children -- ISS-0425's own text is
explicit this is NOT in scope. InstanceSupervisor is placed inside
Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure alongside the other currently-inert
leaf children, matching its CURRENT behavior (an empty
DynamicSupervisor); this is not a claim about which layer it belongs
in once (if ever) a future requirement gives it real children -- left
as an explicitly open question for that future requirement, not
guessed at here.

task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) for REQ-219: validate lib/letflow/design/req219-supervision-layering.md against docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-219 entry (all 10 acceptance_criteria) before this design is eligible to route to ELIXIR-DEV.

checks_performed.20_child_split_and_order: PASS -- independently re-read lib/letflow/application.ex lines 26-134 and re-derived the flat 20-child list by hand. Design section 1.1's 17-item Infrastructure list matches application.ex's children 1-17 verbatim and in the same order (Repo, Ecto.Migrator, Oidcc.ProviderConfiguration.Worker, Registry, Metrics.Registry, Admission, InstanceSupervisor, SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor, SandboxPool, PluginTaskSupervisor, PluginRegistry, Lua.TaskSupervisor, Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor, Wasm.CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor, Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistry, Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistryTaskSupervisor, Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor). Section 1.2's 2-item Pollers list (Scheduler.Poller, ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller) matches scheduler_children/0 + service_task_dispatcher_children/0 exactly. Section 1.3's 1-item Http list (Bandit) matches http_child/0 exactly. 17+2+1=20, every child accounted for exactly once, no omissions or duplicates.
checks_performed.ordering_constraints_iss0224_iss0429: PASS -- ISS-0224: SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor (item 8) precedes {Letflow.SandboxPool, []} (item 9) within Infrastructure's own list, unchanged adjacency. ISS-0429: Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor is the last (17th) child of Infrastructure, and the design correctly argues the ordering guarantee is now structural (a full supervisor boundary between Infrastructure's Supervisor.start_link/3 return and Pollers' own start) rather than list-position-based, which is a strictly stronger guarantee provided Infrastructure is listed before Pollers at the top level (verified true in section 2's 3-element list).
checks_performed.ac2_test_mechanism_scrutiny: FAIL -- traced the exact state transitions of section 4's test procedure step by step. The test (1) lets the real Letflow.Application boot normally (Infrastructure and Pollers both already fully started, in whatever order application.ex's top-level list actually specifies), (2) THEN sets the pollers_init_probe env var, (3) THEN calls Supervisor.terminate_child(Letflow.Supervisor, Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers) + Supervisor.restart_child/2 -- i.e. it manipulates ONLY the already-running Pollers child, never Infrastructure, and never re-runs the actual cold-boot sequence. Because Infrastructure is never terminated, Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor is trivially still registered and alive at every point after the original (real) boot completed, REGARDLESS of whether Infrastructure was originally listed before or after Pollers in Letflow.Application.start/2's top-level children list. Concretely: if a future edit accidentally swapped the top-level list to [Pollers, Infrastructure, Http] (the exact regression AC2 exists to catch), the real application would still boot successfully (Pollers has zero children under config/test.exs's gates, so its wrong-order early start would not crash), Infrastructure would still start second and finish, and this test -- run afterward, against the now-fully-booted system -- would STILL observe a non-nil Process.whereis(Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor) at Pollers' restart-triggered init/1 and STILL pass. The test therefore has zero discriminating power between the correct order and the exact regression it is meant to catch; it only proves 'Infrastructure is up by the time I restart Pollers sometime after the whole app already booted,' which is true independent of original boot order once boot has completed. Section 4's own justification for this ('Infrastructure is never restarted by this action... so the invariant holds for every start of Pollers, whether original boot or later restart') is the flaw restated as a feature: it proves the invariant is preserved ACROSS RESTARTS of an already-correctly-ordered system, not that the ORIGINAL BOOT ORDER was correct in the first place, which is the actual property AC2's text asks for ('at the moment Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers' own init/1 runs' -- read in context of AC2's own first sentence, which is specifically about Letflow.Application.start/2's top-level list index ordering, i.e. real application startup, not an arbitrary later restart). A test that could not fail under the exact ordering regression it exists to guard against is not a passing design for a hard, safety-critical AC.
checks_performed.ac4_test_mechanism_scrutiny: PARTIAL FAIL (folded into the overall FAIL) -- confirmed via grep that no config/*.exs file sets :force_poller_crash or :pollers_init_probe, so section 5's env-gated raise guard added to lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex's handle_info(:tick, state) is inert in every real environment today. However, this codebase has an established, stronger precedent for exactly this class of test-only production seam: lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex lines 226-247 (test_pause_after/test_pause_fun, cited there as matching lib/letflow/design/req021-auth-plug-pipeline.md's OQ-5) gates its test hook behind BOTH (a) a config value AND (b) a separate @activation_test_hooks_enabled? flag resolved once via Application.compile_env/3 at COMPILE TIME, defaulting false, set true ONLY in config/test.exs -- so a compiled dev/prod release can never execute the test path regardless of any runtime Application.put_env/3 call, deliberate or accidental. Design section 5 (and section 4's pollers_init_probe) instead use a bare Application.get_env/3 runtime check with no compile-time gate at all -- its only safety net is 'no config file happens to set this key,' which is weaker than the codebase's own established double-gate convention and does not protect against a future runtime.exs/ops-console/deploy-script Application.put_env/3 call ever reaching this raise in a live release. The design does not follow -- or explain a deliberate, justified departure from -- its own codebase's precedent for this exact scenario.
checks_performed.poller_ex_scope_question: ACCEPTABLE, contingent on the AC4 fix above -- touching lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex for a small, tightly-scoped, disabled-by-default test seam is defensible and within REQ-219's implied scope (the requirement's own 'NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT' list only excludes ISS-0421's internal Poller fix, REQ-220, and InstanceSupervisor's real-children question -- none of which this touches); no requirements.yaml boundary update is needed. This is conditioned on adopting the established double-gate (compile_env + explicit test-hooks-enabled flag) pattern rather than the current bare runtime env check, so REVIEWER is reviewing the same class of seam this codebase has already vetted once, not a novel one.
checks_performed.no_implementation_code: PASS -- grepped the whole design doc for defmodule/def/case/fn/->; every code-shaped fragment is a bare child-spec tuple (e.g. {Task.Supervisor, name: ...}) or a supervisor-opts keyword list, matching the already-accepted req218 no-fenced-code-block style. No function bodies present.
checks_performed.all_10_acs_covered: PASS -- cross-checked against docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-219 acceptance_criteria list verbatim: AC1 (3-child top-level shape) -> section 2; AC2 (Infrastructure-before-Pollers + test) -> section 4 (mechanism present but flawed, see above); AC3 (17-child Infrastructure list + ISS-0224) -> section 1.1; AC4 (2-child gated Pollers, empty-list-ok) -> section 1.2/section 6; AC5 (crash-loop isolation) -> section 3/section 5 (mechanism present but weaker-than-precedent, see above); AC6 (Http owns exactly Bandit) -> section 1.3; AC7 (no config/*.exs changes) -> section 8's last bullet; AC8 (Pollers moduledoc records override+rationale) -> section 3/section 7; AC9 (REVIEWER sign-off content) -> section 7's checklist; AC10 (mix test/compile) -> left to ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-RUNNER as expected, not a design-time artifact.
checks_performed.open_questions_triage: Q1 (exact raise message wording), Q2 (shared test-helper factoring), Q3 (REQ-220 dependency pointer) are all genuinely minor and non-load-bearing -- none constrains any acceptance criterion or leaves an ambiguity ELIXIR-DEV could resolve two different, behaviorally-inconsistent ways. Correctly left to ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-DESIGNER discretion; not a gate issue.

issues: lib/letflow/design/req219-supervision-layering.md section 4 (AC2 ordering-test mechanism): the test restarts ONLY Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers (via Supervisor.terminate_child/2 + restart_child/2) against an already-fully-booted application, while Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure is never touched. This provides zero discriminating power against the exact regression AC2 exists to catch (Infrastructure and Pollers swapped in Letflow.Application.start/2's top-level children list) -- traced step by step: under a swapped-order regression, the real application would still boot successfully (Pollers is empty under config/test.exs's gates) with Infrastructure finishing second, and the design's test -- which only probes AFTER full boot -- would still observe Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor non-nil and still pass. Fix: redesign the test to exercise the REAL cold-boot ordering, not a later single-child restart. The most direct mechanism is to genuinely stop and restart the whole :letflow OTP application in the test (e.g. Application.stop(:letflow) then Application.ensure_all_started(:letflow), or an equivalent full re-invocation of Letflow.Application.start/2's actual Supervisor.start_link/2 call under a fresh, isolated top-level supervisor name so it does not collide with the still-registered production one) with the pollers_init_probe env var set BEFORE that (re-)boot, so the assertion is made against a start sequence where Infrastructure's own start_link genuinely has not run yet at the moment the probe fires if the ordering were wrong. Explain in the design exactly why the chosen mechanism would fail under the swapped-order regression (a concrete counterfactual trace, the same rigor already applied to the ISS-0224/ISS-0429 static-order argument), not just why it succeeds under the correct order.

lib/letflow/design/req219-supervision-layering.md sections 4 and 5 (pollers_init_probe and force_poller_crash test hooks): both use a bare Application.get_env(:letflow, key, default) runtime check with no compile-time gate, relying solely on 'no config/*.exs file sets this key' as the safety net. This is weaker than this codebase's own established precedent for exactly this class of test-only production seam: lib/letflow/repository/activation.ex's test_pause_after/test_pause_fun mechanism (lines 226-247, citing lib/letflow/design/req021-auth-plug-pipeline.md's OQ-5) additionally gates its functional clause behind a separate flag resolved once via Application.compile_env/3 at compile time, defaulting false, set true only in config/test.exs -- making the hook structurally unreachable in any compiled dev/prod release regardless of any runtime Application.put_env/3 call. Fix: adopt the same double-gate pattern for both pollers_init_probe (section 4) and force_poller_crash (section 5) -- an Application.compile_env/3-resolved module attribute (e.g. @supervisor_test_hooks_enabled?, default false, true only in config/test.exs) guarding the functional clause that reads/invokes each env-var hook, in addition to (not instead of) the existing runtime get_env check. If CODE-DESIGNER judges the weaker single-gate gate sufficient for THIS use case specifically, the design must say so explicitly and justify the departure from the activation.ex precedent (e.g. via a REVIEWER-facing rationale paragraph), rather than silently using a weaker mechanism than the one already established and accepted for the same problem.
result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- 2 issues above (1 safety-critical test-design flaw in AC2's mechanism, 1 precedent-inconsistency in AC2/AC4's test-hook gating), rework iteration 1
